evidence.source_sentence: Resulting copolymer was characterized via cyclic voltammetry (CV), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), four probe technique conductivity measurement and UV–Vis spectroscopy.
The IR spectrum was recorded on a Nicolet 510 FTIR spectrometer, where samples were dispersed in KBr.

In the infrared spectrum of P(TMPMT-co-Th) 1697 $\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$stands for the conjugation along the chain. C–O–C stretching peak still existed at $1 2 \overline { { 1 } } 9 \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$, but not as strong as in the monomer. The sharp peak at $7 7 2 \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$indicated the presence of $\mathrm { P F } _ { 6 } ^ { - }$, the dopant anion.
In the infrared spectrum of P(TMPMT-co-Th) 1697 $\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$stands for the conjugation along the chain.

characterizations.result_summary: SEM micrographs of P(TMPMT-co-Th) film show homogenous compact granular structures, which are distinct from pristine polythiophene morphology.

evidence.source_sentence: Resulting copolymer was characterized via cyclic voltammetry (CV), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), four probe technique conductivity measurement and UV–Vis spectroscopy.
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) studies were performed by JEOL JSM-6400.

SEM micrograph of solution side of P(TMPMTco-Th) film showed homogenous compact structures in granular form (Fig. 3(a)). The solution side of film was significantly diferent than that of pristine polythiophene (Fig. 3(b)) which might be considered as a further proof of copolymerization.
Fig. 3. SEM micrographs of (a) P(TMPMT-co-Th) and (b) PTh.

characterizations.result_summary: Measured λ_max of 427 nm, band gap of 2.20 eV, optical contrast of 8%, switching time of 2.0 s for P(TMPMT-co-Th) film

evidence.source_sentence: Resulting copolymer was characterized via cyclic voltammetry (CV), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), four probe technique conductivity measurement and UV–Vis spectroscopy.
Spectroelectrochemical and kinetic studies were performed on Solartron 1285 potentiostat/galvanostat and a HP8453A UV–Vis spectrophotometer.
The film deposited onto ITO coated glass electrode was placed in a UV cuvette for UV–Vis experiment after it is washed with monomer free electrolyte solution.
The % optical contrast (%DT) was measured using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer.

characterizations.result_summary: Measured switching time of 1.4 s, optical contrast of 2% for the ECD

evidence.source_sentence: Dual type electrochromic device (ECD) of P(TMPMT-co-Th) and poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) was constructed. Spectroelectrochemistry, switching ability, open circuit memory and stability of the device were examined by UV–Vis spectroscopy and cyclic voltammetry.
